questions.problem:
Consider the function $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}.$  The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}g(x)}{(x+8)^{7}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{4}+2x})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((x+8)^{6}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{4}+2x-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+8)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}+2x-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+8)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =4{x}^{3}+2-6\cdot \frac{1}{x+8} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}(4{x}^{3}+2-\frac{6}{x+8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{6}}(\frac{(4{x}^{3}+2)(x+8)-6}{x+8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{7}}((4{x}^{3}+2)(x+8)-6) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}}{(x+8)^{7}}(4{x}^{4}+32{x}^{3}+2x+16-6) \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{4}+2x}(2{x}^{4}+16{x}^{3}+x+5)}{(x+8)^{7}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)=2{x}^{4}+16{x}^{3}+x+5.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $y=\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x-1}}{(1-3x)^{6}}g(x)+\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+1)^{x})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-3x)^{5}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-3x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+x\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot (2x)-5\cdot \frac{1}{1-3x}\cdot (-3) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{15}{1-3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{15}{1-3x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{15}{1-3x}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}+\frac{15}{1-3x})+\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}(\frac{2{x}^{2}(1-3x)+15({x}^{2}+1)}{({x}^{2}+1)(1-3x)})+\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}(\frac{17{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}+15}{({x}^{2}+1)(1-3x)})+\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x-1}}{(1-3x)^{6}}(17{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}+15)+\frac{({x}^{2}+1)^{x}}{(1-3x)^{5}}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(x)=17{x}^{2}-6{x}^{3}+15.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $y=\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{2}(g(x)-({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\sqrt{({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{csc}⁡x}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}}{\sqrt{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+4)^{3/2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{1/2}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\cdot 2x-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}(\frac{3x}{{x}^{2}+4}-\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{({x}^{2}+4)^{3}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}(\frac{6x-({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{2({x}^{2}+4)}) \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{2}+4}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}(\frac{6x-({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{cot}⁡x}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(6x-({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\sqrt{({x}^{2}+4)\operatorname{csc}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)=6x.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $y=\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}}.$ The derivative of this function is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{({x}^{2}+2)(11{x}^{2}+24x-2)}{g(x)}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}}{\sqrt[3]{3x+6}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6/3}}{(3x+6)^{1/3}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{2}}{(3x+6)^{1/3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{2}}{(3x+6)^{1/3}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+2)^{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡((3x+6)^{1/3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x+6)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2)-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x+6)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =2\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+2}\cdot 2x-\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{3x+6}\cdot 3 \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{4x}{{x}^{2}+2}-\frac{1}{3x+6}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{4x}{{x}^{2}+2}-\frac{1}{3x+6})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}}(\frac{4x}{{x}^{2}+2}-\frac{1}{3x+6}) \\  & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}}(\frac{4x(3x+6)-({x}^{2}+2)}{({x}^{2}+2)(3x+6)}) \\  & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{({x}^{2}+2)^{6}}{3x+6}}(\frac{11{x}^{2}+24x-2}{({x}^{2}+2)(3x+6)}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+2)(11{x}^{2}+24x-2)}{\sqrt[3]{(3x-6)^{4}}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)=\sqrt[3]{(3x-6)^{4}}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((x-2)^{5})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)-({x}^{2}+3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-2)-({x}^{2}+3x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =5\cdot \frac{1}{x-2}-(2x+3) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{5}{x-2}-(2x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y[\frac{5}{x-2}-(2x+3)]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}[\frac{5}{x-2}-(2x+3)] \\  & =\frac{(x-2)^{5}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}[\frac{5-(x-2)(2x+3)}{x-2}] \\  & =\frac{(x-2)^{4}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}[5-(x-2)(2x+3)] \\  & =\frac{(x-2)^{4}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}[5-(2{x}^{2}-x-6)] \\  & =\frac{(x-2)^{4}}{{e}^{{x}^{2}+3x}}[11+x-2{x}^{2}]\end{aligned}
$$
